architecture.mechanism: Dual-loop disturbance-rejection control — integrating LADRC (Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control) with a cascade FOPIDN controller estimates and compensates load fluctuations, intermittency, and delay effects to maintain bus stability.
architecture.intervention: Add an LADRC-FOPIDN dual-loop controller to the vehicle power management unit (alternator field current regulation plus battery/load bus switching) so intermittent faults and load dumps are actively rejected in real time instead of collapsing the electrical bus.
architecture.expected_effect: Transient voltage/frequency dips during highway operation are compensated, sustaining power to ignition, engine electronics, and DVD player, eliminating sudden total power loss.
architecture.falsification_test: Bench-test the vehicle electrical system with induced intermittent battery/alternator faults at highway load profiles; compare bus voltage retention and engine-shutdown events with vs. without the LADRC-FOPIDN controller — if complete power loss persists, the mechanism is falsified.
